context:
Tiny, surgical change. Remove one line from pyproject.toml, refresh
uv.lock, run fast tests. The risk is essentially zero because chdb-core
is reachable via the existing chdb declarations in the extras that
actually need it. If a future code path wants to import chdb_core
directly, it should declare chdb (which transitively brings chdb-core)
rather than depending on the leaked-into-core declaration.
description:
`chdb-core>=26.1.0` is declared on line 49 of `pyproject.toml` as a CORE
runtime dep. It has zero direct `import chdb_core` sites anywhere in
`benchbox/`, `tests/`, `scripts/`, or `docs/`. `uv tree` shows that
`chdb-core` is a dep of `chdb v4.1.6`, which itself lives in optional
extras (`extras:all`, `extras:clickhouse-local`, `dep-group:dev`).

Net effect today: every minimal install of benchbox pulls `chdb-core`
(a sizeable C++-bundled package, ~tens of MB) even when the user did
not ask for ClickHouse local mode. Moving `chdb-core` out of core deps
trims the install footprint and keeps the optional/required boundary
honest.

Source for this finding: `docs/development/dependency-inventory.md` (F1),
produced by `audit-imported-dependencies-for-elimination`.

anti_patterns.dont: add chdb to core deps to compensate
anti_patterns.why: that would defeat the optionality of ClickHouse

anti_patterns.dont: remove chdb-core from extras as well
anti_patterns.why: chdb depends on it transitively, and uv tree would re-add it; the only goal is dropping the redundant *core* declaration

deferrals.reason: Out of scope; covered by the parent audit-imported-dependencies-for-elimination.
deferrals.resolved_reason: [G4 sweep] superseded: Parent audit-imported-dependencies-for-elimination (DONE 2026-04-15) scopes 'every declared dep... does it belong in the manifest', covering transitive-only core deps. The deferral explicitly delegated to that now-completed parent.
deferrals.summary: Audit other transitive-only deps that may also be in core

preserves.behavior: ClickHouse local extras (`extras:all`, `extras:clickhouse-local`, `dep-group:dev`) continue to install chdb (and therefore chdb-core)
Fast test suite green after the change
No new explicit `import chdb_core` is introduced

verifications.command: uv run -- python -c "import tomllib, pathlib; deps = tomllib.loads(pathlib.Path('pyproject.toml').read_text())['project']['dependencies']; assert not any('chdb-core' in d for d in deps), 'chdb-core still in core deps: ' + str([d for d in deps if 'chdb-core' in d]); print('OK: chdb-core removed from core')"

work_units.summary: Confirm zero direct `chdb_core` imports in shipped source: `grep -rn 'chdb_core' benchbox tests scripts docs`. Document the result in the commit message.
Edit pyproject.toml: remove `chdb-core>=26.1.0` from `[project] dependencies`. Refresh uv.lock with `uv lock`.
Run fast suite to confirm no regressions. Verify chdb-using extras still pull chdb-core transitively: `uv tree --depth 2 | grep -B1 chdb-core`.
